questions.explanation: 'Too many' is used with countable nouns like 'people'.
questions.q: There are ___ people in this room.

questions.explanation: 'Too much' is used with uncountable nouns like 'coffee'.
questions.q: I drank ___ coffee. I can't sleep.
She has ___ friends, so she's never lonely.
He has ___ money, so he can't buy a car.

questions.explanation: 'Too much' is used with uncountable nouns.
questions.q: There is ___ sugar in my tea!

questions.explanation: 'A few' is used with countable nouns like 'students'.
questions.q: Only ___ students came to the party.

questions.explanation: 'Too many' goes with countable nouns: 'too many cars'.
options: There are too much cars here.
There are too many cars here.
There is too much cars here.
questions.q: Which sentence is correct?
I have ___ time. Let's talk later.

questions.explanation: 'Too much' goes with uncountable nouns like 'salt'.
questions.q: She put ___ salt in the soup.
___ people came to the meeting — only five.
He eats ___ chocolate every day.
We have ___ apples. Let's make a pie.

questions.explanation: 'Milk' is uncountable, so use 'a little milk', not 'a few'.
options: I have a little money left.
There is a few milk in the fridge.
questions.q: Which sentence has a mistake?
There are ___ mistakes in your essay!
I need ___ help with this exercise.
___ water is wasted every day.
She has ___ patience, so don't make her wait.
He made ___ noise during the film.
Only ___ sugar, please. I'm on a diet.
There are ___ cars on the road today.
